Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. Leaders of the group of seven democracies say they've agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products,
and they will start with what they called substantial amounts of diesel after that fuel hit record high prices in the U.S.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley says the G7 leaders felt political pressure to release the oil.
Guy-rocketing energy prices are hurting consumers and businesses on the continent and putting so much pressure on governments that are already not very popular.
Europe's diesel prices have more than doubled since the start of the U.S.-Iran war in late February.
In France, Wanna, diesel is $10 a gallon. Farmers, fishermen, truckers, all these categories of workers use diesel.
They're also known to protest and shut down cities and highways, so leaders are really worried about social unrest.
That's NPR's Eleanor Beardsley with our report.
New York's Democratic governor has appointed a special prosecutor in the case of a woman who says she was gang-raped at the Cornell University fraternity in 2024.
As Steve Kastenbaum reports, the investigation was initially closed without any charges being brought.
Governor Kathy Hochul says the young woman was failed by the people obligated to protect her.
I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug. We are ensuring that all the facts of this case are brought into the light.
It will now be up to State Attorney General Letitia James to determine whether any of the seven accused fraternity members will face criminal charges.
We will review the facts, gather evidence, interview witnesses, and if warranted, pursue prosecutions.
The governor says she lost faith in the local prosecutor's ability to handle the case.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum in New York.
This year's Kennedy Center honors are going to be held at Washington's downtown arena instead of the Kennedy Center itself.
A spokesperson announced the change on Friday but did not offer an explanation.
Trump says the center needs safety repairs, and it will only happen if his name is added to the facility.
The Indian pilot who managed to unlock the cockpit door of a fly-to-buy flight this week after he was stabbed is being hailed as a hero, effectively saving the lives of passengers.
NPR's Dia Hadid reports.
The pilot's name is Smit Machar, and Indian TV channels like Republic World and News 18 spared no praise for him.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi video called Machar, who is recovering in a Dubai hospital, and told him the whole country is praying for you.
Machar was stabbed by his co-pilot while on a fly-to-buy flight packed with Israeli nationals.
He told the prime minister that he had collapsed but told himself he had to get up to open the cockpit door.
Otherwise, he said, passengers would lose their lives.
After Machar unlocked the door, passengers rushed in and overpowered the other pilot.
And two passengers, who happened to be pilots, safely landed the plane.
Dia Hadid, NPR News, Mumbai.
It's NPR News.
Metal health counselors are warning about the risks of prediction market sites.
As NPR's Bobby Allen reports, clinicians say problem gamblers are relapsing with apps like Kalshi and Poly Markets.
Prediction market sites are surging.
Kalshi's data shows the $60 billion bet on the platform last month was up 2,000 percent from 2025.
But unlike online sports books like FanDuel and DraftKings, prediction markets do not honor so-called self-exclusion registries.
These are lists maintained by states that automatically ban gambling addicts from using betting sites.
Mental health experts say it is a loophole that many bettors are falling into after coming across Poly Market or Kalshi's ubiquitous ads.
Kalshi in a statement says it invests in responsible trading, including its own self-exclusion list.
But state officials say as long as Kalshi and Poly Market stay unlicensed by states, there are fewer consumer protections.
Bobby Allen, NPR News.
Scientists in Argentina are trying to figure out just why unusually high numbers of baby whales are washing up dead along the Patagonian coast.
The lead researcher Friday said that bacterial infections could be to blame. They're now testing tissue samples to see if that theory holds up.
They also want to know if warming waters from climate change could be playing a role.
CBS's lead analyst for the network's NFL coverage is no longer with the network.
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo was arrested in July and charged with operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
He was suspended and later pleaded no contest to the charge. He had been the lead analyst since 2017.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
